correctness.rationale: For every strict input order, min{x_i,max(x_{i-1},x_{i+1})} selects one of at most three input coordinates into each output, giving row-selector Q. The exact complete-pair Gini quotient for a selector equals the maximum binary cut ratio q(n-q)/[s(n-s)] by layer-cake/coarea and triangle inequality; generic line integration extends the branch upper bound globally and local perturbations realize it. Every source multiplicity <=3, giving for n>=6 a two-case upper bound 3(n-3)/(n-1): for 3s<=n/2 optimize q<=3s, otherwise q(n-q)<=n²/4 and s(n-s)>=5n²/36. The explicit single-coordinate input witness realizes threefold replication at n>=6. n=2 operator maps both sites to their common minimum; n=3,4,5 satisfy the listed small cut bounds. Independent enumeration of every strict-order chamber and all nontrivial cuts for n=2..8 reproduced exactly 0,1,4/3,3/2,9/5,2,15/7. Thus the all-dimensional proof is valid apart from its stated finite-domain scope.
